newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds slipped to a lower close on Friday, following Bunds and U.S. T-bonds down after sharply higher than expected U.S. non-farm payrolls data, which sparked fears the U.S. economy might be overheating.
But dealers said that compared to other markets guilder bonds were holding up quite well, with new buyers stepping in as prices fell.
"We saw a lot of buying on dips, actually the market is quite buoyant, relatively speaking," one dealer said, adding players appeared to have been covering shorts at lower levels.
"Generally the market is doing quite well with some good cash buying," another dealer agreed. "We were able to place quite a lot of 2005 and 2006 paper."

The 10-year spread to Bunds looked to be stabilising at around -13 to -14 basis points, the dealer added. The yield on the 10-year benchmark 6.25 percent bond finished at 14 basis points under the April Bund, compared with -12 on Thursday.
Other dealers cited brisk trade in the 1999/2000 area, while 2004 paper was also heavily traded.
"Swaps were holding up the belly of the market -- the 2000-2002 area," one said.
